source: literature fallback: Materials Project entries read from the public website (CC BY 4.0), accessed 2026-08-07, plus standard experimental values for Nb
note: These are the only real DFT numbers in this project. BCC Ti and BCC Zr are high-temperature phases, mechanically unstable at 0 K in DFT; their anchors are still well-defined static-lattice values. a0 values are derived from the reported nearest-neighbor bond length d via a0 = 2 d / sqrt(3) (Ti, Zr) or from the reported EOS volume (Nb).

Ti.citation: Materials Project mp-73, Ti (Im-3m), K_VRH 105 GPa, Ti-Ti bond 2.82 A; https://materialsproject.org/materials/mp-73 (CC BY 4.0)

Zr.citation: Materials Project mp-41, Zr (Im-3m), K_VRH 89 GPa, Zr-Zr bond 3.10 A, density 6.58 g/cm3; https://materialsproject.org/materials/mp-41 (CC BY 4.0)

Nb.citation: Materials Project mp-75, Nb (Im-3m), K_VRH 174 GPa, EOS V0 18.34 A3/atom; https://materialsproject.org/materials/mp-75 (CC BY 4.0)

experimental.citation: room-temperature experimental values for Nb, e.g. C. Kittel, Introduction to Solid State Physics, 8th ed. (a = 3.30 A; B = 170 GPa)
